decisions.reason: The product builds on existing capabilities but has limited public commitment, so escalation of commitment is moderate, making a drop less likely than for distant products but more likely than for flagships.
The product had a quantified launch and builds on established capabilities, indicating some public commitment and sunk investment, which leads management to continue it.

As a publicly announced flagship that builds on established capabilities, dropping it would write off visible investment and expose earlier commitment as a mistake, so escalation strongly favors keeping it.
The firm founded a new brand and presented it as a focus, creating high public commitment and sunk costs, so escalation of commitment makes dropping it very unlikely.

The product is distant from the established offer and was only briefly mentioned without public commitment, so there is little invested and little to justify, making dropping more likely under escalation logic.
